verdict: Accepted rigorous partial progress; no unconditional proof or compliant counterexample.
accepted_major_results: Finite-energy smooth graph transformations of actual inverses are exact inverse competitors, including structured natural-exponent cutoffs.
One-sided full-class minimality gives a finite mixed inverse-cube moment for every feasible rank-one-connected nonnegative endpoint.
An admitted nonminimizer has no uniformly positive same-trace repair changing only one fixed target component, in any fixed direction.
Exact weighted-core exclusion persists under controlled annular limits; audit refinement permits strong W1,infinity convergence to a C1 positive-angular-J profile.
Bounded-relative inverse additions and controlled rank-one endpoints provide actual finite-energy comparison intervals.
One admitted inverse has a smooth additive direction with finite energy only at amplitude zero.
Fixed-trace volume bounds reference-truncation thresholds; barrier-normalized excess loses uniform unweighted strain coercivity.
Smooth volume-preserving identity-trace maps with arbitrarily small total excess can have orientation-reversing affine blends.
scope_limits: No general high-level finite-energy truncation or determinant-raising repair has been constructed.
Generic compact W1,9/5 inverse additions remain unresolved; structured graph transformations are conditional on finite final energy.
The mixed inverse-cube moment is weighted by an explicitly feasible endpoint Jacobian and does not itself yield unconditional inverse-cube integrability.
The fixed-direction repair obstruction concerns admitted nonminimizers, a fixed target direction, and an all-domain bound.
Annular tangent exclusions assume strong convergence, positive exponents with sum greater than three, and positive limiting angular Jacobian.
No unconditional gradient higher integrability, global determinant lower bound, or compliant counterexample.
No exhaustive literature or originality claim.
coordination_corrections: Local determinant-average convergence now specifies L6-Lebesgue points of the gradient.
